hiw_meta_title: How AutoRig Works: Auto Rig Any 3D Model in Seconds
hiw_hero_lead: Drop in a 3D model, a picture, a picture of a car or anything else. AutoRig builds the skeleton and the skin in seconds, retargets animation clips at once and opens one viewer for the rig, the animation, the checks and the downloads.
hiw_product_desc: The pipeline is designed for batch processing and repeatable results: it removes the need for users to understand the technical details of rigging and engine assembly, turning model upload into a simple "input → ready output" service.
hiw_product_highlight: Upload your model and get a fully prepared character ready for production use.
hiw_formats_desc: The system automatically recognizes the format, correctly imports it, and brings it to a unified working state so that further stages are performed stably and identically.
hiw_openpose_desc: One of the key elements of quality is automatic detection of character reference points using OpenPose. The system can work with up to 137 markers:
hiw_openpose_humanoid: Automatic detection works best on humanoid forms (characters with familiar anatomy): in this case, the pipeline most confidently determines limbs, hands, and proportions, which directly improves the quality of subsequent rigging and deformations.
hiw_tpose_title: Automatic Model Preparation for Correct T-Pose
hiw_tpose_intro: For the automatic rig to be created correctly and produce predictable deformations, the pipeline prepares the model and brings it to a technically correct state:
hiw_tpose_orientation: Model orientation: normalization of "forward/up" direction, bringing to correct position relative to scene axes so that rigging, animations, and engine export work without surprises.
hiw_tpose_scale: Scale and unit auto-check: the system verifies correct scale and brings the model to expected units so the character has the right size, animations don't look "sped up/slowed down" due to scale.
hiw_tpose_limbs: Leg and arm position correction: adjusting the pose toward cleaner T-pose logic. Important for stable joint detection, correct segment lengths, and quality skinning.
hiw_tpose_fingers: Finger detection and preparation: separate work with hands to improve finger rig accuracy and reduce deformation artifacts during animation.
hiw_tpose_result: Result: the model becomes "ready for rigging": correctly oriented, at the right scale, and in a pose suitable for automatic skeleton construction.
hiw_skeleton_intro: After preparation, the pipeline automatically performs the key technical part:
hiw_skeleton_create_desc: A bone structure is formed for the main body parts (spine, legs, arms, head), with correct connections and hierarchy.
hiw_skinning_auto_desc: Vertex weights are distributed across bones so that when the skeleton moves, the model deforms naturally without "breaking".
hiw_skeleton_result: This transforms a static model into a fully animatable character without manual routine work.
hiw_animations_intro: The pipeline delivers results in two forms to cover different workflows:
hiw_baked_desc: Ready for import into game engines. Convenient format for game project integration: clips play back stably and predictably.
hiw_controlrig_desc: Fully suitable for manual animation in Blender. Important if you need to manually adjust pose/movement, create unique animation for a task, or quickly make artistic edits without rebuilding the entire pipeline.
hiw_animations_result: The system supports both the "production" path (engines) and the "artistic" path (manual animation).
hiw_unity_intro: For Unity, the pipeline creates a unitypackage ready for use in Unity HDRP projects:
hiw_unity_1: Model and animations prepared for correct import
hiw_unity_2: Materials and textures brought to HDRP-render compatible form
hiw_unity_3: Result is convenient to connect to projects without manual assembly and lengthy setup
hiw_unity_result: This reduces integration time and decreases typical errors when transferring a character to Unity.
hiw_video_intro: After assembly, the system automatically creates a realistic video:
hiw_video_1: Shows the final character appearance with correct lighting and materials
hiw_video_2: Shows how the rig and deformations work in motion
hiw_video_3: Quick quality assessment without manual scene and render setup
hiw_video_result: Video serves as quick quality control of the final assembly: it's clear what came out "at the output" and where refinement is needed if necessary.

img2rig_lead_h2: One picture in, a whole character out
img2rig_lead_p1: Most image-to-3D tools stop at a mesh. You get a static model, and rigging it is still your evening. AutoRig treats the picture as the start of the whole pipeline: the image becomes a textured 3D model, the model gets a skeleton and skin weights, and an animation library is retargeted onto it. All of it arrives as a single task with a single progress page.
img2rig_lead_p2: The routing decision is made once, right after upload. The site looks at your picture and decides whether it shows a character that can carry a skeleton. If it does, you get generation plus rigging. If it does not — a vehicle, a prop, a building, a character whose limbs are fused into the body — you still get a proper PBR 3D model, because the model is what you paid for either way.
img2rig_examples_h2: Characters generated from a single image

img2rig_how_h2: How it works, step by step
img2rig_how_intro: Four stages run without you touching anything after the upload.
img2rig_step1_d: Open the AutoRig home page and drop a PNG, JPG or WEBP file on the upload zone. One image is one character. You need to be signed in, because generation is charged to an account.
img2rig_step2_t: The site decides what it is looking at
img2rig_step2_d: Detection checks whether the image shows a character in a T-pose or A-pose with limbs clear of the torso. This decides the route only: riggable pictures go to generation plus rigging, everything else goes to generation alone.
img2rig_step3_d: The picture goes to the GPU farm and comes back as a textured mesh with PBR materials, retopologised into usable geometry rather than a raw scan-like surface.
img2rig_step4_t: The model is rigged and animated
img2rig_step4_d: A skeleton is fitted, skin weights are solved, and the animation library is retargeted onto the new character. The task then publishes GLB, Unity FBX, the HDRP unitypackage, Blender files and a preview video.
img2rig_deliver_h2: What lands in the task when it finishes
img2rig_deliver_intro: A finished character task publishes a full delivery set, not a single file. The examples on this page shipped between 9 and 17 artifacts each.
img2rig_deliver_glb_d: The web-native format. It plays in the browser viewer on the task page and drops straight into three.js, Babylon, Godot or any glTF pipeline.
img2rig_deliver_fbx_d: The skeletal mesh with the retargeted animation set baked in, ready for Mecanim.
img2rig_deliver_unity_d: A Unity package with materials wired for the High Definition Render Pipeline, so the character is not pink on import.
img2rig_deliver_blender_d: The scene as Blender sees it, for weight painting, retopology touch-ups, or exporting to something the list above does not cover.
img2rig_deliver_video_d: A rendered clip of the character playing its animations - the same videos embedded on this page.
img2rig_pose_p: The detector is looking for a readable body, not for art quality. A rough sketch in a clean T-pose beats a beautiful render of a character folded into a dramatic action pose.
img2rig_pose_li1: The character faces the camera, standing upright and roughly centred.
img2rig_pose_li2: Arms are away from the torso - straight out for a T-pose, or angled down for an A-pose.
img2rig_pose_li3: Legs are separated, with a visible gap between them.
img2rig_pose_li4: The whole body is in frame, including hands and feet.
img2rig_pose_li5: The background is plain, or at least does not blend into the silhouette.
img2rig_pose_fallback_h3: And when the picture is not a character
img2rig_pose_fallback_p: Nothing is rejected. A picture that cannot carry a skeleton still produces a textured PBR 3D model - you simply get the model without the skeleton and the animations. That is a routing decision made per picture, never a failure message.
img2rig_batch_p: Drop a handful of images and each one becomes its own task, queued together. The upload zone accepts a multi-file selection and starts them in sequence, so a set of concept sheets can turn into a set of rigged characters in one pass. Drop a single file and you land on that task's page; drop several and you land on your task list.
img2rig_price_h2: What it costs, and what is free
img2rig_price_free_p: Uploading a 3D model you already have and running the rig costs nothing and needs no account. Watching the result costs nothing either - the browser viewer, the animation playback, the preview video and the public gallery are all open. AutoRig is free to run and free to look at.
img2rig_price_paid_p: Unlimited Monthly covers model generation from pictures and the complete model workflow without a per-model limit. Existing credit balances remain valid and can still be used until they are exhausted.
img2rig_price_packs_p: The single paid web plan is $20 per month and renews automatically until cancelled. It includes unlimited model creation, private models, and public gallery visibility controls.
img2rig_price_refund_p: A pipeline retry does not create a second charge or subscription event.
img2rig_price_nofree_p: An account is required so the subscription and privacy controls stay linked to the correct owner. Existing purchased credits are preserved.
img2rig_faq_q1: Do I need a 3D model to start?
img2rig_faq_a1: No. That is the point of this page - a single picture is enough. If you already have a GLB, FBX or OBJ, upload it directly instead and skip generation entirely.
img2rig_faq_q2: Does the character have to be in a T-pose?
img2rig_faq_a2: A T-pose or an A-pose both work, as long as the limbs are clear of the body. The pose decides whether rigging is attempted; it never decides whether you get a model.
img2rig_faq_a3: The examples on this page took roughly 20 to 50 minutes end to end, including time spent waiting in the farm queue. The task page shows live progress, and you can close the tab - the task keeps running.
img2rig_faq_q4: What if I upload something that is not a character?
img2rig_faq_a4: You get a textured PBR 3D model of whatever it was. Detection routes the job, it does not reject it.
img2rig_faq_q5: Can I rig several characters at once?
img2rig_faq_a5: Yes. Select several images in the upload zone and each becomes its own task, charged separately.

faq_title: AutoRig FAQ: rig, animate and export any 3D model
faq_lead: Short answers about uploading, the viewer and the AI agent, rigging for characters, animals, hands and cars, animation, textures and export.
faq_q_viewer_open: What happens after I upload a model?
faq_a_viewer_open: Every task opens in its own Unity WebGL viewer. It starts on a black scene at once and plays the stages (voxels, erosion, bones, rig) while the mesh loads, then loads the chosen environment scene. When the rig is ready, the animations play from the bar at the bottom, and the AI agent chat sits in the corner.
faq_q_viewer_camera: How do I move the camera?
faq_a_viewer_camera: The right mouse button pans and the middle button orbits; left-drag also orbits, and Shift + left pans. The wheel changes the lens, Ctrl + wheel moves closer. F frames the model, F11 goes full screen, F12 saves a screenshot and F1 lists every key. On a phone, drag with one finger and pinch with two.
faq_q_viewer_tools: What are the icons around the viewer?
faq_a_viewer_tools: Left: model, rig, bones, blueprint, voxels, framing, auto camera and the outliner. Right: the look of the scene. A click switches an icon to its next preset, the last step turns it off, and holding the icon opens its detailed settings. Bottom left: the channels, keys 1–0. A right click opens a menu with this FAQ.
faq_q_agent_what: What can the AI agent do?
faq_a_agent_what: The agent lives in your task's viewer. It looks at the model, decides what to do next and uses tools: it checks joints, feet and skinning, repairs frames, adds animations, changes materials, light and scene, and renders images and videos of the result.
faq_q_agent_talk: How do I talk to the agent?
faq_a_agent_talk: Type in the chat under the video window in the bottom-right corner, in any language. Ask in plain words: “check the feet”, “make her wave”, “make the eyes glow”. Quick-reply chips suggest next steps, and renders and videos appear right in the chat.
faq_q_agent_sees: Does the agent see what I see?
faq_a_agent_sees: It knows which layer and clip are on screen and whether the bones are shown, and it can drive the viewer for you: play a clip, show a layer, move the camera, change materials, weather and time of day.
faq_q_agent_original: Will the agent change my original file?
faq_a_agent_original: No. Your upload stays as it is. Edits are saved as new versions on top of it, and material changes can be undone.
faq_a_rig_how: The fast rig builds the skeleton and skin from the model's geometry in seconds, using the template of its category, and the animation clips are retargeted at once. Quality checks (joint placement, skin tears, limb collisions, numeric deformation QA) run in the background of the viewer. Humanoids get a standard humanoid skeleton that animation tools and game engines understand.
faq_q_rig_inspect: How do I inspect the bones and the skinning?
faq_a_rig_inspect: Press F8 or the bones icon to see the skeleton over the model. Play a clip, press Space to stop on a frame and step with the arrow keys. Channel 0 colours the body parts, and the outliner (9) hides or isolates any part.
faq_q_rig_fix: A joint is in the wrong place. Can I fix it?
faq_a_rig_fix: Yes. Press B for Blueprint mode and move the bones; symmetry mirrors your edit to the other side. The rig is rebuilt 15 seconds after your last edit, or at once with the re-rig button, and the correction goes into every animation. You can also ask the agent to check the feet, the knees or a single frame.
faq_a_rig_models: People, stylised and anime characters, animals, birds, creatures, hands and cars. Upload GLB, FBX, OBJ or a ZIP with textures, or generate a model from a picture or text.
faq_a_anim_which: A rigged character comes with ready motions such as idle, walk, run, jump, wave, dance, punch and look around; every other category has its own clip library, for example walk, trot and gallop for a horse. They play from the bar at the bottom of the viewer, and the agent can add more on request.
faq_a_anim_retarget: Retargeting moves a motion made for one skeleton onto yours while keeping your character's proportions. Your joint corrections are carried into every retargeted clip.
faq_q_anim_frame: Can I fix one bad frame?
faq_a_anim_frame: Yes. Press Space to stop the clip, find the frame on the slider and press the wrench: the frame is smoothed with its neighbours and flips in the clip are repaired.
faq_q_edit_what: Can I edit the model itself?
faq_a_edit_what: Yes. Pick any object, material or body part in the outliner (9) or click it in the scene, then change its colour, metalness, smoothness and glow. The eye icon hides parts so you can look inside.
faq_q_edit_agent: Can the agent edit the model for me?
faq_a_edit_agent: Describe the change and the agent makes it: recolour clothes, make eyes or armour glow, try other materials. Every material change can be undone.
faq_q_edit_scene: Can I change the scene around the model?
faq_a_edit_scene: Yes: the post-processing look, depth of field, volumetric light, weather, time of day, stages such as a studio or a cathedral, and a radial pulse on Alt. Each is one click on the right toolbar.
faq_q_gen_image: Can I make a 3D character from a picture?
faq_a_gen_image: Yes. Upload a picture: AutoRig builds a 3D model from it, rigs it and opens it in the viewer with animations. A picture of a car goes through the vehicle conveyor instead.
faq_q_gen_text: Can I describe a character in words?
faq_a_gen_text: Yes. Write what you want to see; the character is generated from the description, then rigged and animated the same way.
faq_q_gen_video: Can I start from a video?
faq_a_gen_video: Yes. Send a video and the agent uses it as a reference for the character and its movement.
faq_q_gen_media: Can the agent make images and videos of my character?
faq_a_gen_media: Yes: renders, turntables and short videos of the character in a scene. They appear in the chat next to the viewer.
faq_q_ch_keys: How do I check textures and materials?
faq_a_ch_keys: Use the keys 1–0 or the icons in the bottom-left corner: 1 full shading, 2 albedo, 3 normals, 4 metallic, 5 roughness, 6 emission, 7 object IDs, 8 material IDs, 9 the outliner, 0 body parts.
faq_q_ch_ids: What are object and material IDs?
faq_a_ch_ids: Each separate object or material gets its own flat colour, so you see at once how the model is split and which parts share a material.
faq_a_ch_kept: Yes. A model's own textures are never lost: materials, textures and UVs are kept through rigging, and the PBR maps (base colour, normal, metal-roughness and emission) show up in the channels.
faq_a_export_formats: The rigged, animated model downloads as GLB and FBX. USDZ, a ZIP bundle, a Unity package and a Blender file are offered too, and static copies are available as OBJ.
faq_q_export_engines: Does it work in Unity, Unreal and Blender?
faq_a_export_engines: Yes. The FBX imports as a humanoid in Unity and as a skeletal mesh in Unreal, and the GLB opens in Blender, three.js and other web viewers. A ready Unity package and a Blender file come from the same task.
faq_q_export_rights: Can I use the result commercially?
faq_a_export_rights: Yes, if you own the rights to the source model. AutoRig adds the skeleton, skinning and animations and claims no ownership of your model.
faq_a_export_api: Yes. Tasks can be created, tracked and downloaded through the API; the developer page has the details.

faq_a_cat_pose: Any pose works. When a biped stands on one leg or steps, the leg on the floor sets the bone lengths for the other, so both legs get the same lengths. If the file already has a skeleton or an animation, its own rest pose is used first.

faq_a_veh_what: Yes. Drop a picture of a car on the home page. The vehicle conveyor segments it into body, wheels, doors, hood, trunk, hatches, glass, lights and bumpers, models each part as its own 3D object and assembles a rigged car.

faq_a_veh_parts: Every part is isolated and restored as a whole object, and the viewer lists them in the Parts panel. For each part you accept it, redraw it or order it as a 3D model. The body is drawn as a bare shell without doors, hood and glass, so those parts open and move on their own.
faq_q_veh_wheels: How are wheels, body and doors made correct?
faq_a_veh_wheels: Each wheel is normalised to a cylinder collider that matches its own shape. The body is corrected to left–right symmetry with a free-form deformation (FFD) lattice, and the doors are hinged.
faq_q_veh_driver: Is there an interior and a driver?
faq_a_veh_driver: Yes. The cabin has a seat, a steering wheel, pedals and a gear stick, and a rigged driver is seated at them by IK.
faq_q_veh_paid: Are paid 3D services used for cars?
faq_a_veh_paid: The free farm is the default. Paid 3D clouds (Tripo and Hunyuan cloud) run only when you press their explicit button.
faq_q_rig_quality: How is the rig quality kept up?
faq_a_rig_quality: Every model that once broke a rig becomes a regression test, and every engine release has to pass these autotests before it goes live. Rig quality comes before speed.
faq_q_anim_library: Where do the clips come from?
faq_a_anim_library: For each category, reference videos of the gaits and actions are generated and the motion is extracted once. The clips are then retargeted automatically onto every new rig, with a numeric QA check on each clip. Procedural clips are the fallback.
faq_q_anim_custom: Can I add my own clips?
faq_a_anim_custom: Yes. Custom clips can be added in the viewer to the task's clip set, and they are retargeted onto your rig like the built-in ones.
faq_q_ch_auto: What if my model has no textures?
faq_a_ch_auto: It gets PBR textures automatically (albedo, roughness, metallic, normal and emissive), made from the model's own projections. The textured model is what the vision checks and the previews use.
faq_a_site_lang: The site is available in English, Russian, Chinese, Hindi and Persian (right to left). English pages have no prefix; the others live under /ru/, /zh/, /hi/ and /fa/.
faq_q_site_report: How do I report a bad rig?
faq_a_site_report: The Telegram notice of a finished task has defect buttons, for example a wrong model transform, a torn mesh after skinning or elbows that are too wide, and you can reply with text too. A report is recorded and checked, and the fix goes into the engine for the whole category, not into one model.

hiw_flow_title: From upload to a rigged, animated model in seven steps
hiw_flow_intro: The same conveyor runs for every task. You see each stage in the viewer as it happens.
hiw_s1_text: Drop a 3D model (GLB, FBX, OBJ or a ZIP with textures), a picture, a picture of a car, or text. One upload zone takes all of them. A picture becomes a 3D model first and then goes on to the rig. A picture of a car goes to the vehicle conveyor.
hiw_s2_text: The engine reads the geometry and picks the rig category. It fills the model with voxels, erodes them to find the inner axis of every limb, places the bones and binds the skin. This takes seconds.
hiw_s3_text: Clips from the category library are retargeted onto the new rig right away: walk, idle, run, and for horses trot and gallop. Every clip passes a numeric deformation check. You can add your own clips in the viewer.
hiw_s4_text: A model's own textures are never lost. A model without textures gets PBR textures automatically (albedo, roughness, metallic, normal, emissive), made from its own projections. The textured model is what the vision checks and the previews use.
hiw_s5_text: While you watch the model move, the checks run in the background of the viewer: joint placement, skin tears, limb collisions, deformation numbers and a vision review of the textured model. Rig quality comes before speed.
hiw_s6_text: Every task opens in one viewer with an agent chat. Edit the skeleton in blueprint mode, or confirm it when the viewer offers. The confirmation is never required: the animation does not wait for it.
hiw_s7_text: Download the model as GLB, FBX, USDZ, a ZIP, a Unity package or for Blender. The same rig works in engines, in Blender and on the web.

seo_tpose_description: T-pose rig without the T-pose: AutoRig rigs a model in any pose, uses the file's bind pose first and offers the skeleton for confirmation in the viewer.
tpose_lead: You do not have to put a model into a T-pose before you upload it. AutoRig rigs the pose you give it, in seconds, and offers the skeleton for confirmation in the viewer.
tpose_cta: Rig a model in any pose
tpose_f2: Bind pose from the file first
tpose_answer_h2: Do you need a T-pose to rig a character?
tpose_answer_p1: No. A T-pose is a fine input, but AutoRig does not require it. A model in an A-pose, a relaxed stance, a step or with a raised leg is accepted as it is.
tpose_answer_p2: The fast rig builds the skeleton and the skin from the geometry in seconds, and the animation clips are retargeted at once. The target is a rigged, animated model within one minute from pickup.
tpose_cases_h2: What AutoRig does with each pose
tpose_c1_d: The skeleton is fitted straight to the geometry.
tpose_c2_d: A relaxed stance or arms down: the skeleton is traced from the posed geometry, with no pose-correcting step first.
tpose_c3_t: A skeleton or an animation inside the file
tpose_c3_d: The pose is a baked frame, so the file's own rest pose (its bind pose) is used instead of a fit to the posed mesh.
tpose_c4_t: Feet that do not stand side by side
tpose_c4_d: A step or a raised leg: the leg on the floor is the reference for the other leg.
tpose_c5_d: A horse, a bird, a hand or a car has no T-pose to match. Each category has its own skeleton template.
tpose_how_h2: How a posed model is rigged
tpose_s1_d: AutoRig looks for a source skeleton or an animation. If it finds one, the pose is a baked frame and the file's bind pose is used, not a fit of the posed mesh.
tpose_s2_d: With no skeleton in the file, the skeleton and the skin are built from the geometry in seconds, and the animation clips are retargeted at once.
tpose_s3_t: Uneven legs use a reference leg
tpose_s3_d: When the feet are not side by side, the standing leg sets the bone lengths and the joint order for the other leg.
tpose_s4_t: The skeleton is offered, not demanded
tpose_s4_d: The viewer offers the skeleton for confirmation in blueprint mode. The animation is made without waiting for it, and the quality checks run in the background.
tpose_leg_h2: The standing leg is the reference
tpose_leg_p1: When a biped's feet do not stand side by side, the leg whose foot is on the floor sets the topology and the lengths: hip to knee, knee to ankle, ankle to toe.
tpose_leg_p2: The other leg is traced along its own points, but its joints are placed at the reference lengths. Both legs get the same bone lengths and the same joint order, whatever the pose. The rig never shortens or stretches one leg to fit a pose.
tpose_leg_p3: Symmetry follows the voxels. The mirror overlap of the model's solid decides whether the blueprint opens with symmetry on; an asymmetric model keeps its own bones in both legs.
tpose_leg_ref: Reference leg: its foot is on the floor
tpose_leg_traced: Traced leg: its own path, joints at the reference lengths
tpose_leg_lengths: L1 hip to knee · L2 knee to ankle · L3 ankle to toe
tpose_bp_h2: Check and edit the skeleton in blueprint mode
tpose_bp_p: Press B in the viewer to open blueprint mode and move bones with symmetry. The model is re-rigged 15 seconds after your last edit, or at once with the button. You can also leave the skeleton as it is: the confirmation is offered, never required.
tpose_cap1: A biped with its skeleton and the skin weight of every bone.
tpose_cap2: A bird: the wings are rigged as wings. Rest pose and clip frames from the rig check sheet.
tpose_cap3: A horse has no T-pose to match: it gets an equine skeleton and clips that pass numeric QA. The sheet shows the gallop.
tpose_cap4: A single hand has no T-pose either: it gets per-finger joints and hand clips.
tpose_other_p: Quadrupeds, horses, birds, hands and cars are rigged with templates of their own. Read the animal rigging page or the guides index to pick your category.
tpose_q1: Do I need a T-pose to auto rig a character?
tpose_a1: No. Any pose is accepted. A T-pose or an A-pose is a fine input, but not a requirement.
tpose_q2: What if my file already has a skeleton or an animation?
tpose_a2: AutoRig checks for that first. When a source skeleton or an animation is there, the pose in the file is a baked frame, and the file's own bind pose is used instead of a fit to the posed mesh.
tpose_q3: My character takes a step or stands on one leg. Will the legs match?
tpose_a3: Yes. The leg on the floor is the reference. The other leg is traced along its own points, with its joints at the same bone lengths and in the same order.
tpose_q4: Do I have to confirm the skeleton before I get the animation?
tpose_a4: No. The viewer offers the skeleton for confirmation in blueprint mode, but the animation is made without waiting for it.
tpose_q5: How long does a rig take?
tpose_a5: The fast rig builds in seconds. The target is a rigged, animated model within one minute from pickup, while the quality checks continue in the background of the viewer.
tpose_q6: Is a T-pose or an A-pose better?
tpose_a6: Neither is required. The T-pose vs A-pose guide explains what each pose changes.
